comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## OPERATOR RULING — this does NOT gate epic e369

Asked directly whether e369's closure should be gated on fixing this, the operator ruled **follow-up, do
not gate**. Recorded here because the operator's earlier ruling on the three J11-surfaced defects (751e,
2b16, 88d9) went the STRICTEST way, so a reader could reasonably expect the same here; this one was
decided differently, deliberately.

The distinction that justifies it: the behaviour introduced by 2b16 fails **SAFE**. G5 declines to unlink
when the pair's net-active relation is not the one whose peer link vanished, so it never removes a link
the peer still carries — the alternative would be destroying local data. What remains is a
**non-convergence**: the removal re-emits and re-declines every pass, visible only as a log line. That is
a materially different class from the J11 defects, every one of which silently produced a WRONG result.

And the proper fix is a design pass in its own right, not a patch: expressing "remove only the `blocks`
edge between A and B" means changing the public `rebar.unlink(id1, id2)` signature or introducing a new
lower-level seam. Pulling that into e369 would delay DC delivery for a narrow case that already fails in
the safe direction.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## OPERATOR-RATIFIED DECISION (2026-08-04)

The operator ratified the relation-scoped fix, resolving the ticket's 'Options (deliberately not pre-decided)' section in favor of option 1, with a design constraint that keeps the public surface backward compatible:

1. Add a RELATION-SCOPED removal seam at the graph layer — removal keyed on (target_id, relation), symmetric with graph/_links.add_dependency.
2. Make the reconciler's inbound link-removal path use it, so G5's decline case instead CONVERGES by removing exactly the mirrored relation. The safety invariant is kept: no link the peer still carries is ever removed — a removal naming a relation with no matching net-active local link is a logged no-op.
3. CLI `unlink` gains an OPTIONAL relation argument (`rebar unlink <id1> <id2> [relation]`); with no relation the existing pair-scoped most-recent behavior is UNCHANGED (backward compatible). The library facade `rebar.unlink` gains the same optional `relation=None` keyword.

This supersedes the earlier follow-up ruling's open design question ('changes the public rebar.unlink signature or needs a lower-level seam') — the answer is BOTH, backward-compatibly: a lower-level graph seam plus an optional-arg extension that leaves existing call sites untouched.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## RCA (Phase 1, confirmed)

Root cause: write/remove key asymmetry in the link store API.

- WRITE is relation-scoped: graph/_links.py::add_dependency is idempotent per (target_id, relation) ('if a net-active LINK with the same (target_id, relation) already exists' — docstring), so one ordered pair can hold e.g. blocks AND relates_to simultaneously.
- REMOVE is pair-scoped: _commands/unlink.py::_get_link_info returns 'the most recent net-active link for target' (no relation key), and rebar.unlink/unlink_core expose no relation parameter.
- Consequence: rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py::_inbound_unlink_one (guard G5, change 1276 / bug 2b16) asks _get_link_info what a pair-scoped unlink WOULD remove and declines with a WARNING when that relation differs from the relation whose peer link vanished. Correct fail-safe direction, but the decline is permanent: inbound_differ._diff_link_removals_inbound re-emits the removal every pass and G5 re-declines it, so the two systems never converge for a double-related pair, with no operator-visible signal beyond a log line.

Legitimacy: defect (silent non-convergence of the reconciler's inbound removal contract), confirmed live by the coexistence of two relations per pair (idempotency key in add_dependency) — G5 is not dead code. Fix design ratified by the operator (see previous comment). Caller sweep: _inbound_unlink_one is the only G5 caller; rebar.unlink callers (CLI dispatcher, MCP unlink_tickets, reconciler) all pass no relation and keep identical behavior under the optional-arg extension.

# Inbound link removal never converges when a pair holds two relations (unlink is pair-scoped)

## Context / Problem

Links are WRITTEN keyed on `(target_id, relation)`: `graph/_links.py::add_dependency` is
idempotent per `(target_id, relation)`, so one ordered pair CAN hold two net-active
differently-related deps (e.g. `blocks` + `relates_to`). But removal is pair-scoped:
`rebar.unlink(id1, id2)` takes no relation argument and `_commands/unlink.py::_get_link_info`
returns "the most recent net-active link for target". Change 1276 (bug `2b16-9be0-a8f5-41d9`)
therefore added guard G5 in `rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py::_inbound_unlink_one`,
which declines + logs when the pair's net-active relation does not match the relation whose
peer link vanished.

**How a remove record reaches G5 despite G4 (traced).** In a normal bidirectional pass,
G4 (`inbound_differ.py::compute_inbound_mutations`, the action-aware same-pass link
suppression) drops an inbound remove whenever the outbound differ emitted a link mutation for
the same pair — and `outbound_links.py::_diff_links` usually re-emits an ADD for a
still-local, peer-absent dep, so in THAT case the pair "converges" by outbound re-adding the
peer-deleted link and G5 is never reached. But the outbound ADD is deduped
**direction-agnostically on `(vendor_type, target_key)`** and "intentionally NOT deduped on
`relation`" (`_diff_links` docstring + `already_present` check), while the inbound removal
differ compares in per-relation LOCAL vocabulary (`link_direction.py`: `blocks` and
`depends_on` BOTH map to vendor type `Blocks`). So when a local dep's vendor type collides
with a remote link of the same vendor type in the OTHER direction — e.g. local dep
`blocks → K` while the remote pair holds an inward `Blocks` link (which reads as `depends_on`
in local vocabulary) — that remaining same-vendor-type remote link keeps the outbound ADD
deduped (`already_present` → skip), outbound emits nothing for the pair, `ob_entry`'s
`link_add_keys`/`link_remove_keys` are empty, and the inbound remove record survives to G5.
The same holds for any pass where the outbound differ emits no link mutation for the pair
(e.g. inbound-only application of records). In those G5-reached cases the decline IS
permanent when the pair's most-recent net-active relation differs from the vanished one: the
removal record re-emits and re-declines on every subsequent pass, so inbound link removal
never converges for that double-related pair. This fix targets exactly that G5-reached path;
the G4-suppressed path (outbound re-add wins) is out of scope and unchanged. (Verified at
runtime in a scratch store: one ordered pair holds `blocks` + `relates_to` net-active
simultaneously; `blocks` + `depends_on` on one ordered pair is rejected by the cycle guard;
pair-scoped `rebar.unlink` removes the most-recent link.)

**Relation to 2b16's fail-safe ruling (removal-convergence is deliberately re-enabled).**
The operator ratified converting the G5 decline into a relation-scoped removal (see the
ratified-decision comment). The residual exposure — `managed_refs` marks a ref managed the
instant it is created locally, so a managed-but-never-pushed local link whose outbound ADD
is permanently deduped by the direction-agnostic vendor-type check is state-indistinguishable
from a genuine peer deletion — is PRE-EXISTING, not introduced here: today, when such a
never-pushed link is the pair's most-recent net-active link, G5's relation match PASSES and
the pair-scoped unlink already removes it. This change only makes the outcome
order-independent (the exactly-named relation is removed instead of "whichever is most
recent, else decline forever"). It never removes a relation the record did not name, and a
record naming a relation with no matching net-active local link removes nothing. The proper
discriminator (persisted peer-link history distinguishing never-pushed from peer-deleted) is
a design pass of its own, filed as ticket `a4bd-4ca8-c44f-49bb` (linked `discovered_from`
this ticket) and deliberately out of scope here.

## Approach (operator-ratified 2026-08-04 — see comment)

Make removal symmetric with the write path, keyed on `(target_id, relation)`:

1. **Graph-layer relation-scoped removal seam** — `graph/_links.py` gains
   `remove_dependency(source_id, target_id, tracker_dir, relation)`, symmetric with
   `add_dependency`: validates the relation, finds the most recent net-active LINK with
   exactly that `(target_id, relation)`, writes the UNLINK event through the shared locked
   write seam, and removes the reciprocal link for `relates_to`. The net-active replay in
   `_commands/unlink.py::_get_link_info` gains an optional `relation=` filter (default `None`
   keeps pair-scoped behavior) so the seam and the CLI stay in lockstep on one replay.
2. **Reconciler convergence** — `_inbound_unlink_one` uses the relation-scoped removal, so
   the G5 decline case converges by removing exactly the mirrored relation. The safety
   invariant is preserved positively: when the named relation has NO net-active link locally,
   the removal is a logged no-op and no other relation's link is ever removed.
3. **CLI backward-compatible optional relation** — `rebar unlink <id1> <id2> [relation]`.
   With a relation, removal is relation-scoped; with no relation, the existing pair-scoped
   most-recent behavior is byte-for-byte UNCHANGED. `rebar.unlink` (library facade) gains the
   same optional `relation=None` keyword.

Strict TDD: RED behavioral tests first, then the implementation turns them GREEN.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/graph/_links.py` — add `remove_dependency` (relation-scoped removal seam) and an
  UNLINK event writer mirroring `_write_link_event`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/unlink.py` — optional relation on `_get_link_info`, `_write_unlink`,
  `unlink_core`, `unlink_cli`; usage text updated.
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` — `rebar.unlink(id1, id2, relation=None, ...)`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` — `_inbound_unlink_one`
  performs relation-scoped removal instead of the permanent G5 decline.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_link_removal_2b16.py` — the G5 mismatch
  test is revised to the new contract (still asserts the other relation's link survives and
  a mismatching removal with no matching local link removes nothing); a new test proves the
  double-related pair converges.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_unlink_relation_scoped_e39f.py` — new: two-relation pair
  behaviors for the seam, the facade, and the CLI (including no-relation backward compat).
- `src/rebar/_cli/help/unlink.txt` — the pinned `--help` text the CLI actually prints
  (served by `_cli/_help.py::subcommand_help`) gains the optional relation.
- `docs/cli-reference.md` — machine-generated from the help files under a CI drift gate;
  regenerated with `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`.
- `docs/user-guide.md` — the one-line `rebar unlink` description gains the optional relation.

Out of scope (owned elsewhere): MCP `unlink_tickets` signature, binding_store.py, jira
fetcher.py issuelinks merge, completion attestation/signing, show-command rendering.

## Testing

Behavioral, through public entry points:
- Happy path: pair holds `blocks` + `relates_to`; relation-scoped removal of `blocks` leaves
  `relates_to` net-active (and vice versa), asserted via `rebar.show_ticket` deps.
- Reconciler: a double-related pair whose peer dropped one relation converges — the mirrored
  relation's dep is gone after `_inbound_update_apply_links`, the other survives, and the
  apply is counted (`applied == 1`); re-apply is an idempotent no-op.
- Safety/negative: removal naming a relation with no net-active local link removes NOTHING
  (G5's invariant, asserted positively) and is a logged no-op; `unlink` with an invalid
  relation errors; `unlink` with no relation keeps the existing most-recent pair-scoped
  behavior (existing tests stay green unmodified except the revised G5 mismatch test).
- Edge: relation-scoped removal of `relates_to` also removes the reciprocal link.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test proves a pair CAN hold two differently-related net-active deps (checked: the new
      lifecycle test creates `blocks` + `relates_to` on one pair and asserts both appear in
      `show_ticket` deps).
- [ ] A peer deletion of ONE relation in a two-relation pair reaches a defined end state: the
      exactly-mirrored relation's link is removed and the reconcile converges (checked: new
      2b16-file test drives `_inbound_update_apply_links` and asserts the named relation's dep
      is gone, the other remains, and a second apply is a counted-zero no-op).
- [ ] G5 never removes a link the peer still carries — asserted positively (checked: revised
      mismatch test shows a removal naming a relation with no matching net-active local link
      leaves the pair's other link intact and removes nothing).
- [ ] `rebar unlink <id1> <id2>` with NO relation argument behaves exactly as before (checked:
      all pre-existing unlink tests pass unmodified; a new test pins most-recent pair-scoped
      removal).
- [ ] Targeted tests, `make lint`, and `make typecheck` pass in the worktree venv (checked:
      command output recorded in ticket comments).
- [ ] Mutation-checked: re-introducing the pair-scoped call in `_inbound_unlink_one` turns the
      convergence test RED; verdicts recorded on the ticket.
